Add the no-worker-identifiers rule and its email check (#292)

Add the adopter-owned rule under .claude/rules/external/ that bars any
worker email address, account identifier, seat label, or other
third-party identifier from every public or potentially public
surface, and link it from the Adopted governance section of
.claude/CLAUDE.md.

Add tools/test-no-worker-identifiers.py, which reads the raw bytes of
the stored blob of every entry that git ls-files --stage lists and the
name of every path it lists, and takes every candidate address around
every at sign, so an exempt candidate cannot hide another, with work
that grows linearly with the file. It reads each blob that the index
names through 1 git cat-file batch call, never the working copy, so no
attribute, filter, encoding, such as a working-tree-encoding of
UTF-16LE, or state of the working copy changes what is scanned; a
tracked symbolic link is scanned by its own stored target text, not by
the file that it points to. 2 exemptions, each tested on a candidate
folded to lower case, so each holds in any letter case: (1) the
candidate is exactly the maintainer's own email address; (2) the
domain of the candidate is reserved for documentation: its last label
is invalid, test, or example, or it is, or ends with a dot and then,
example.com, example.org, or example.net. An at sign passes only when
every candidate that the scan reads at it is exempt, under either
exemption, or when it lies in a file on a line that the reviewed
exact-line allowlist holds for that file. So, off such a line, an
address passes only when each shorter domain that it holds, ending
after 2 or more letters that follow a dot, gives an exempt candidate
as well. 1 exact-line allowlist entry covers the URL-userinfo fixture
in tools/test-release-links.py; a stale entry fails.

Only a hit in the content of a file names a line: that failure names
the file, the line number, and a digest of the match. A hit in a path
name names the path and a digest of the match, and no line; a stale
allowlist entry names its file, its position, and a digest of its
text, and no line; and the fail-closed failures below name no line and
no digest of a match. No failure holds the matched text or the line.
A path whose name holds a match is named in each of its failures only
by a digest of the path name; any
other path name is printed with each character that is not printable,
such as a line feed, a carriage return, or the escape byte of a
terminal escape sequence, and each backslash written as a backslash
escape, so each failure is 1 line. A red run prints every failure in
full, 1 to a line after a count, never through a list comparison that
unittest shortens. A failed git ls-files or git cat-file call, a git
that cannot start, an empty listing, and a blob that cannot be read are
failures, never a skip, and each gives only a fixed category with the
exit code of git, the errno name or type of the error, or a fixed word
for the blob (missing, not a blob, or unexpected reply), never a
diagnostic of git, the message of an exception, the error text of the
system, or the path of the repository or of git; a failed git call
names no path, and a blob that cannot be read is named by its
repository path, or, when its path name holds a match, only by a
digest of the path name, as every failure names its file.
Each caught example in the suite is assembled at run time, so its
source holds no matchable text.

Run the suite as a named step of the Orchestration registry workflow,
name it in the header of that workflow, mirror it in
tools/run_all_checks.sh, and record the new sha256 of that script in
tools/test-run-all-checks.py, which pins it.

Spellings that the scan catches, a closed set: outside the exemptions
and the allowlisted lines, the scan catches an address when, and only
when, its text holds all 4 of these parts, in any letter case: a local
part of 1 or more ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores, percent
signs, plus signs, or hyphens; right after it, the ASCII at sign
itself, the 1 byte 0x40; right after that, a domain run of ASCII
letters, digits, dots, or hyphens; and in that run, a dot with at least
1 byte of the run before it and 2 or more ASCII letters right after it.
Every other spelling of an address passes, whatever its encoding or
inserted character. Examples only, not a complete list, of other
spellings that pass where they leave those 4 parts incomplete: an
address split across lines; an address assembled by code; an address
written with the word at; an at sign outside ASCII, the fullwidth or
the small commercial at sign; an at sign written as an HTML character
reference, decimal, hexadecimal, or named; a percent-encoded at sign;
an at sign written as a backslash escape; an at sign written as
quoted-printable; a space, a tab, a carriage return, a less-than sign,
or a zero-width space right after the at sign; a local part that ends
in a letter outside ASCII, a tilde, an exclamation mark, or an
apostrophe; a quoted local part; a domain written with letters outside
ASCII; a domain written as a literal in square brackets; an underscore
in the domain; a zero-width space inside the domain; a soft hyphen
inside the domain; a zero-width joiner, a zero-width non-joiner, a word
joiner, or a byte order mark inside the domain; a dot of the domain
written as an HTML character reference, decimal, hexadecimal, or named;
a percent-encoded dot of the domain; a dot of the domain written as a
backslash escape; a dot of the domain written as quoted-printable; a
dot of the domain written as the word dot, bare or in square brackets;
a fullwidth or an ideographic full stop in place of a dot of the
domain; and a space before a dot of the domain. The suite pins each of
the 4 parts and each example with its own subtest, named with the words
of these lists, and 1 case of the suite fails when the lists in its own
docstring and the names of those subtests differ.

Residual: the check covers the email class only, and within it only the
closed set of spellings above. A seat label, a bare account handle, or
a numeric account identifier passes it, because a committed pattern
that names a real label would itself publish the label; those forms
rest on the rule, on the standing line that every QA and drafting brief
carries, and on any scan the maintainer keeps outside the repository.
An untracked file, the file that a tracked symbolic link points to,
and the content of a submodule are not read; a tracked symbolic link
is scanned only by its own target text. A file kept outside git, for
example by Git LFS, whose blob is a pointer, is scanned only as its
stored pointer, so an address in the file that the pointer names
passes. An address inside compressed or encoded binary content passes,
since the scan neither decompresses nor decodes, unless that content
holds the address as it is. A surface that
is not a file in this tree, such as a pull request title, description,
or comment, is not reached, and tools/check-pr-text.py carries no
identifier pattern today. The suite pins each of the 3 forms that name
no address with its own subtest, named for the form, compressed or
encoded content with its own case, and each place that is not read
with its own case. The digest of a match or of a path name lets
a reader who already holds a guess of the address confirm the guess.
A path name is held back only from the output of the suite: git and
other steps that list files can still print it. On a red run, unittest
also prints a traceback for each failed case, which holds the absolute
path of the suite file in the checkout, and a failed self-check can
print the values that it compared, the path of its temporary folder
among them, so a checkout path or a temporary folder path that holds
an address reaches the CI log. A label that leaked into the history of
an older pull request and was removed later is held for the maintainer
and is out of scope for the rule's enforcement.

Accepted false failures: a legitimate new third-party address is
caught and needs a maintainer decision; email-shaped text that is no
address is caught and is reworded to a reserved documentation domain,
or is added to the allowlist after review; a fixture address at a
reserved domain that also holds a shorter domain that is not reserved,
such as 1 at mail.corp.example.com or 1 that appends the label example
to an ordinary domain, is caught and is reworded to a reserved domain
with no such shorter domain; and an action pinned to a version tag in
which a dot is followed directly by 2 or more letters, such as
v1.2.3-alpha.beta.1 or v2.0.0-rc.ab, is caught, since a domain then
ends after those letters, unless every domain that the tag ends is
exempt, as in v1.2.3-pre.test.1, whose letters form a reserved last
label, or v1.0.0-rc.example.com, while a tag whose every dot is
followed by a digit, such as v1.2.3-rc.1, passes.
